chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from someone else from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who rented land from another man, so he said, 'Its rent is such and such, on the condition that I cultivate it. If I do not cultivate it, I will give you that.' So he did not cultivate it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He may take it if he wishes to leave it (uncultivated), and if he wishes not to leave it (uncultivated), he may not take it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on rent if the tenant fails to cultivate the rented land?
ai.summary: Reported by Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (AS), this hadith clarifies the flexibility in agricultural lease contracts (muzara'ah), granting the landowner the discretionary right to enforce or waive the cultivation condition if the tenant fails to plant. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic principle of respecting contractual autonomy and the specific stipulations agreed upon by parties, rather than imposing rigid penalties for non-cultivation. It highlights the practical application of ijarah in agrarian societies, ensuring fairness while allowing for mutual agreement on consequences.
